# Generalized Linear Models

- [Response distributions and link functions](#response-distributions-and-link-functions)
- [Counts, rates, and overdispersion](#counts-rates-and-overdispersion)

## Response distributions and link functions

- Normal, binomial, and Poisson GLMs
- Logistic regression, prior scale, separation, and interpretation

Agresti 5.1–5.3

## Counts, rates, and overdispersion

- Poisson and negative-binomial models; exposures and offsets
- Choose a response model using prediction and substantive constraints

Agresti 5.4–5.5; selected 5.2 examples

# Hierarchical and Multilevel Models

- [Exchangeability and partial pooling](#exchangeability-and-partial-pooling)
- [Varying effects and repeated observations](#varying-effects-and-repeated-observations)

## Exchangeability and partial pooling

- No pooling, complete pooling, and partial pooling
- Hyperpriors and the distinction between empirical and full Bayes

Agresti 5.6–5.7; old-syllabus hierarchical core

## Varying effects and repeated observations

- Varying intercepts and slopes; group-level prediction
- Generalized linear mixed models and repeated measurements

Agresti 5.7–5.8

# Criticism and Communication

- [Check assumptions at every level](#check-assumptions-at-every-level)
- [Planned Python demonstration](#planned-python-demonstration)

## Check assumptions at every level

- Prior sensitivity, posterior predictive checks, and new-group prediction
- Use basic sampler diagnostics before trusting a computed posterior

Formal computation and diagnostics follow in Posterior Computation

## Planned Python demonstration

- Compare pooled, separate, and hierarchical fits to one dataset
- Explain shrinkage and predictive uncertainty for a small group

No companion notebook released yet
